subject: Scale-to-Save renewal: tiered commit options and transient credits
messages:
From: Lina Ortiz <lina@stellarretail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Scale-to-Save renewal: Q4 forecast & ask

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing our renewal conversation and I wanted to share an updated forecast and a few asks so we can lock something in before our fiscal close. Attached is our forecast for Q4 + Q1 (Stellar_Renewal_Forecast_Q4-Q1.xlsx). High level: our usage is expected to grow ~2.8x across two new product teams (recommendation engine, support automation).

Three things we're hoping Redwood can help with:
- A three-month price hold on current unit rates while we ramp (to avoid mid-quarter sticker shock).
- A transient credit pool to cover initial overages during onboarding (we estimate ~500k token-equivalent in month 1).
- A path to scale: add two additional seats (teams) with committed capacity, but we want flexibility to reallocate commit between teams without penalty in the first 90 days.

Our procurement lead Evan (cc'd) will handle PO logistics. Can you sketch a few commercial options we can review internally? We're aiming to sign by the end of the month.

Thanks —
Lina Ortiz
Head of AI Platform, Stellar Retail
Lina Ortiz | lina@stellarretail.com

Attachment: Stellar_Renewal_Forecast_Q4-Q1.xlsx (forecast workbook)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina@stellarretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scale-to-Save renewal: tiered commit options and transient credits

Lina — appreciate the context and the deck. We're excited by the growth projection and have a few structured options that balance predictability for Stellar with runway to scale. Quick summary below; attaching a draft term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v1.pdf) to start the paperwork conversation.

Proposed commercial options (high level):
1) Scale Commitment (12 months) — Recommended for predictable unit economics
   - Commit: baseline 12-month commit equal to current run-rate * 2.0 (adjusted for forecast)
   - Pricing: tiered discount bands (15% off list up to band 1; 22% off list once commit > band 2)
   - Onboarding credits: 2 months of transient credits (applied monthly) to cover early overages (capped at 550k token-equivalent)
   - Reallocation window: allow commit reassignment between teams within first 90 days with written notice (no penalty)

2) Ramp & Hold (6 months) — Shorter commitment, price protection
   - Commit: 6-month capped commit with option to convert remaining term to dedicated capacity
   - Pricing: smaller initial discount (10%) + 3-month price hold on unit rates for overage pricing
   - Credits: 1 month onboarding credit pool

3) Dedicated Pilot + Burst Credits — for teams that will need guaranteed latency
   - Dedicated reserved pool for priority workloads; separate burst credits bucket to absorb spikes
   - Custom pricing (higher base, but lower overage unit cost)

Operational notes:
- Credits will be invoiced as account credit line for offset; we can show amortization on monthly invoices.
- Any discount >20% requires finance approval and an approved deal rationale (Marissa / Ben, assigning for review).

Next steps:
- Marissa/Ben: can you review the attached term sheet and indicate what needs escalation?
- Lina/Evan: confirm preferred option and we will issue a redline-ready DocuSign. I can hold a 30-minute slot Thursday or Friday for a quick commercial readout.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Commercial Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | diego@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood_term_sheet_v1.pdf (draft term sheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scale-to-Save renewal: tiered commit options and transient credits

Diego — adding commercial constraints and a suggested counter:

Thanks for the clear options. Two internal points to surface before we go to legal/finance:
- Discount bands: anything that results in >25% blended discount across year needs VP finance sign-off. We can provide up to 20% standard discount within the commit bands; anything above should be tied to an absolute committed $ value (not just % uplift).
- Credits treatment: prefer credits amortized monthly; do not allow unapplied credits beyond 6 months. Also we need to cap total transient credits at an absolute dollar amount (recommend $75k) for accounting clarity.

Suggested commercial counter (short):
- 12-month Scale Commitment as Diego recommended but with blended discount 18% (first 6 months 22% to help ramp; months 7-12 at 14%).
- Onboarding credits: 3-month credit pool capped at $75k; credits applied monthly to invoices.
- Reallocation: allow commit reallocation between teams in first 60 days (we can extend to 90 days if we include minimums per team after 60 days).

Ben — can you run the modeled financials (attach pricing_model_playbook.xlsx) and confirm if $75k cap + the 22%/14% cadence keeps margin thresholds acceptable? If so, Diego - we can push this to legal as a redline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing_model_playbook.xlsx (internal pricing model)
